Fred Love

Democratic candidate for Governor, Arkansas · Challenger

Arkansas state senator (District 15); listed by Ballotpedia as a government administrator

Fredrick "Fred" Love is a Democratic state senator from the Little Rock/Mabelvale area. He served in the Arkansas House from 2011 to 2023 and has been in the state Senate since 2023. He announced his run for governor in June 2025, beat Supha Xayprasith-Mays in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, and faces Republican incumbent Sarah Huckabee Sanders and Libertarian Colt Shelby on November 3, 2026.

Where Love stands

Education / LEARNS Act and Education Freedom Accounts
Says his first priority is to stop public education funds from going to private entities. Says he would issue an executive order to end the LEARNS Act and would not administer Education Freedom Accounts.
Maternal and child health
Argues that Arkansas is doing a bad job of protecting mothers and children for a state that calls itself pro-life, and calls for more focus on maternal health.
Prisons / Franklin County prison project
Questions the cost of the proposed Franklin County prison project and the state's spending priorities.
Taxes and cost of living
Questions the state's focus on tax cuts and says spending should put more weight on cost-of-living pressures for Arkansans.
Economy and communities
Says his campaign is focused on protecting public schools, empowering communities, and driving inclusive economic growth across the state, including for small business owners.

Background

  • Arkansas State Senate, District 15 (2023–present; term ends January 2027)
  • Arkansas House of Representatives (2011–2023): District 35 2011–2013, District 29 2013–2023
  • Minority Leader, Arkansas House of Representatives (2019–2021)
  • Democratic nominee for Governor of Arkansas (won March 3, 2026 primary)
  • Bachelor's degree, University of Arkansas at Little Rock (1999); graduate degree, University of Arkansas at Little Rock (2004)
  • Occupation: government administrator (per Ballotpedia)
